values.STACK: a modular Wayland bar for Hyprland, written as a Rust 2024 Cargo workspace (the `cranky` binary and library plus the member crates `cranky-unsafe` and `cranky-time`), with hexagonal ports and adapters inside feature-sliced design, a reactive signal hub, Lua and Rhai widget scripts, forbid-level lints, arch-lint layer rules and a 200-LOC file limit
FINGERPRINT_FILES: - Read `clippy.toml` (the identifier allow-list, the test-only relaxations, `allowed-duplicate-crates`)
- Read `arch-lint.toml` (the layer scopes and the rules between them)
- Read `Justfile` (the `check` gate and the recipes it runs)
- Skim `tests/architecture.rs` (the structural gate: lint tables, zero exceptions, LOC limits, layer rules)
values.ARCH_VOCAB: feature slices (`src/features/`) and shared units (`src/shared/`), layers (`domain`, `ports`, `adapters`), ports and adapters, the composition root (`src/app/`), the `SignalHub` and its signals (`SignalKind`), modules as actors (`AnyModulePort`, `EventLoop`), Lua and Rhai widget scripts, the render pipeline (VNode diff, taffy layout, tiny-skia paint, shm buffer), newtypes and value types, state keyed by `MonitorId`
ARCH_RULES: - `domain` and `ports` never import `adapters` or `app`; `features` and `shared` never import `app` (`arch-lint.toml`, checked by `arch_lint::check!()` in `tests/architecture.rs`)
- `src/app/` is the composition root: it builds the adapters, wires them to the ports and starts them; nothing depends on it
- `unsafe` code lives only in `crates/cranky-unsafe`; the `cranky` crate forbids `unsafe_code`
- A change to the scripting API is made in both the Lua and the Rhai adapters (`src/shared/scripting/adapters/`) and covered by the same tests in `src/app/builtins/tests.rs`
- Visibility follows `AGENTS.md` "Public surface": an item is only as visible as its uses
DOMAIN_EXAMPLES: - **Action verbs**: "switch workspace", "render a module", "reload a style", "subscribe to a signal"
- **Integration surfaces**: Hyprland IPC sockets, D-Bus (MPRIS, StatusNotifierItem), Wayland layer-shell and shm buffers, the Lua and Rhai script API
values.DATAFLOW_EXAMPLE: Hyprland event socket → `HyprlandAdapter` signal loop → `SignalHub` hyprland channel → each subscribed module's `EventLoop` → script `render(monitor)` → VNode diff → taffy layout → tiny-skia paint → shm buffer
ENTITY_RULES: - **Fields are private** (`-`) and exposed through getters (`+`), as `AGENTS.md` convention 4 requires.
- **Identifiers are newtypes**: ids and names wrap their primitive (`WorkspaceId`, `MonitorName`), as the existing domain does.
- **Errors are types**: one `thiserror` `<<error>>` enum per module or adapter, with its variants (`AGENTS.md` convention 5).
- **Ports belong to the slice that needs them** (`ports/`), and adapters implement them (`adapters/`). Ports get no `Debug` supertrait.
- **Exported types are `Debug` and documented with their intent** (`AGENTS.md` "Public surface").
- **Per-monitor state is keyed by `MonitorId`**: multi-monitor is a first-class dimension.
- **Boundary shapes** (Hyprland JSON DTOs, D-Bus values, script tables) are modelled only in the adapter that parses them.
- **Placement respects the 200-LOC limit**: under `src/features/` and `src/shared/`, a unit that would outgrow one file is a directory of small submodules.
APPROACH_SECTIONS: - [Value types, invariants, per-monitor state; key decisions and rationale]
- [Which feature slice or shared unit owns what; ports declared; how `src/app/` wires the adapter]
- [Which `SignalKind` carries the change, who subscribes, which task runs it]
- [Changes visible to Lua and Rhai widgets, made in both adapters, or "None"]
- [`thiserror` enums per module or adapter; how an error surfaces: module error signal, log, boot error]
- [Hyprland IPC, D-Bus, Wayland, rendering; what crosses an adapter]
- [Unit tests with hand-written fakes and `block_on`; integration tests against a private `dbus-daemon` or headless `sway` when an adapter changes]
STRUCTURE_OUTPUT: 3. New crate dependencies: [crate = version, which slice uses it, why] or "None"
1. [`arch-lint.toml` scopes or rules to add or confirm]
2. [Files that must split to stay within 200 production LOC]
values.OPERATION_ORDER: shared value types → slice domain → ports → adapters → script API (Lua and Rhai together) → `src/app/` wiring → widgets and styles → boundaries → docs → verify
OPERATIONS_EXAMPLE: 3. Constructor: `new(name: impl Into<String>) -> WorkspaceName` — [validation, if any]
4. Behaviour: [getters and methods, each with purpose and signature in prose]
5. Tests: [behaviour cases, named after the behaviour]

2. Parsing: [boundary DTOs, kept inside the adapter]
4. Tests: [unit tests with a fake provider; an integration test in `tests/integration/` when it talks to a real server]

### 6. Docs - an intent-stating doc on every exported item; `AGENTS.md` when a rule changes
values.NORMS_BASELINE: `AGENTS.md` applies in full (Conventions, Hard constraints, Architecture, Testing)
NORMS_LINES: 2. Errors: [error enums and messages specific to this change]
3. Naming: [identifiers of three or more characters outside the allow-list; unprefixed CSS classes]
4. Visibility and docs: [the narrowest visibility for each new item; the intent each doc states]
6. Tests: [what is unit-tested, what needs an integration test]
SAFEGUARD_LINES: 2. Multi-monitor: [state keyed by `MonitorId`; behaviour with zero, one and several monitors]
3. Architecture: [layer rules; no `app` import from features or shared; `unsafe` only in `cranky-unsafe`]
4. Lints: [`just lint` and `just doc-check` pass with zero exceptions]
5. Errors: [exact error enum variants and Display messages]
6. Script API: [Lua and Rhai behave the same; the same tests in `src/app/builtins/tests.rs`]
7. Performance: [no blocking inside an `EventLoop`; render and refresh cost; `just bench-check`]
8. Size: [every touched file under `src/features/` or `src/shared/` within 200 production LOC]
9. Tests: [required unit and integration tests; line coverage stays at 80% or more]
CODING_NORMS: - `AGENTS.md` "Hard constraints" is the full list; these are the rules generation breaks most often
- Private fields with getters; newtypes for ids and names; `thiserror` errors per module or adapter

- No `as`, unchecked arithmetic or string slicing anywhere, tests included; no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!`/indexing outside tests (`clippy.toml` relaxes those, and `print`/`dbg`, in tests): use `get()`, `TryFrom`, `checked_*`/`saturating_*` and `Result`
- Identifiers of three or more characters, except `x`, `y`, `id`, `tx`, `rx`, `dx`, `dy` and `px`, tests included; name a binding after what it holds

- Each item only as visible as its uses (`pub(super)`, `pub(in crate::…)`, `pub(crate)` only inside a `pub` module chain); every exported item has a doc that states its intent, and every exported type a `Debug` impl
- No `#[tokio::test]`, `#[tokio::main]`, `#[tracing::instrument]` or `mockall`: tests use `crate::test_utils::block_on`, ports get hand-written fakes, spans are explicit
- `#[must_use]` on constructors and getters, `const fn` where Clippy asks for it
- At most 200 production LOC per file under `src/features/` and `src/shared/`: split into submodules, never allowlist
- CSS classes are not prefixed with the module name (`.container`, `.item`)
- A scripting API change goes into both the Lua and the Rhai adapter
TEST_NORMS: - Unit tests live next to the code in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` (or a `tests.rs`/`tests/` submodule); shared helpers are in `src/test_utils.rs`
- Async code is driven by `crate::test_utils::block_on`, never `#[tokio::test]`
- Ports are replaced by hand-written fakes (`Fake*`), never mockall; assert on behaviour, not call counts
- A test fails when the logic it covers changes incorrectly
- A D-Bus or Wayland adapter change also gets an integration test in `tests/integration/` (private `dbus-daemon`, headless `sway`, `grim`)
- Line coverage stays at 80% or more (`just coverage-check`)
values.CHECK_DESC: fmt-check, lint, doc-check, arch-check, loc-check, test, deps-check and workflows-check; add `just coverage-check` and `just bench-check` when the change can affect coverage or the benchmarks
values.COMMIT_REF: `Refs #<n>` in commits; only the pull request body says `Closes #<n>`
values.GATE_RULE: SPDD is for issues whose Effort on the Project board is 5 or more.
values.GATE_READ: `gh project item-list 7 --owner jaoppb --limit 1000 --format json`, then the `effort` of the item whose `content.number` is `<n>`
values.EXEMPT_RULE: `AGENTS.md` "SPDD" exempts `type:spike` issues: a spike explores, so there is nothing to design yet.
values.TAXONOMY_RULE: `AGENTS.md` "Issues, branches and commits" requires exactly one `type:*` label, at least one `area:*` label, the release milestone and an open parent unless the issue carries `epic`. Read them with `gh issue view <n> --json labels,milestone,parent`.
values.BOARD_START: Move the issue's card to In progress by hand on the Project board (https://github.com/users/jaoppb/projects/7): no `just project-sync` rule moves a card there yet (#97).
values.BOARD_AFTER: after the pull request opens, and again after the merge, run `just project-check`, then `just project-sync` (it needs the `project` scope: `gh auth refresh -s project`).
values.LINT_SUPPRESSIONS: `#[allow(...)]`, `#[expect(...)]` or `#![allow(...)]`, and no macro that emits one (`#[tokio::test]`, `#[tokio::main]`, `#[tracing::instrument]`, `mockall`)
values.DEPS_RULE: A crate that appears twice in `Cargo.lock` is listed in `allowed-duplicate-crates` (`clippy.toml`) and in the `skip` entries of `deny.toml` with its reason, and `just deps-check` passes
values.MEMORY_RULE: durable pages only when the user asks, as the ai-memory block in `AGENTS.md` says
